title: treehouse config.json
description: The global treehouse configuration, read from $TH_CONFIG or ~/.th/config.json. Top-level settings are the defaults for every repository; a repos entry overrides them for the repository whose main worktree lives at its path, and the repo's own .thrc overrides that.

version.description: Config schema version. Run `th migrate` to update an older file.

repos.description: Per-repository overrides, matched by the main worktree's path: the first entry whose path resolves to the same directory wins.

update_check.description: Let `th --version` query GitHub for a newer release. Top-level only, never part of a repos entry or a .thrc, so a repository can never turn on network calls.

repo.description: Settings for the repository whose main worktree lives at path.

name.description: What {repo} expands to in path templates for this repository. Empty means the main worktree's directory basename.

path.description: The filesystem path of the repository's main worktree. A leading ~ expands to the home directory; symlinks are resolved before matching.

worktree_dir.description: Path template placing new worktrees. {repo} and {branch} are substituted and a leading ~ expands to the home directory. Defaults to ~/worktrees/{repo}/{branch}.

default_base.description: The ref new branches start from when the branch exists neither locally nor on origin. Empty means the current HEAD.

branch_prefix.description: Prepended to branch names `th add` creates, joined with prefix_separator: "peter" gives "peter/fix-login".

prefix_separator.description: Joins branch_prefix to the branch name. Empty means "/".

copy_hooks.description: Copy the repository's git hooks into newly created worktrees. Only relevant when core.hooksPath points inside the worktree (husky's .husky, say); a plain .git/hooks is already shared by every worktree.

copy_files.description: Paths or globs, relative to the main worktree, of untracked files (".env", say) to copy into newly created worktrees. Files git tracks are never copied — the checkout already placed them. A repos entry or .thrc replaces this list rather than adding to it; [] disables copying.

link_files.description: Paths or globs, relative to the main worktree, of untracked files or directories to symlink rather than copy into newly created worktrees — a shared node_modules, say, so it costs nothing and stays shared. A repos entry or .thrc replaces this list rather than adding to it; [] disables linking.

vscode.description: VS Code integration settings. Layers merge this object key by key, so setting one key here keeps the rest of the inherited object.

open.description: Open the worktree in VS Code after `th add` creates it. An effective open always beats auto_cd.

workspace_file.description: Write a .code-workspace file into each new worktree, named "<workspace_prefix><branch>.code-workspace".

workspace_prefix.description: Prepended to the generated workspace file's name.

window_title.description: Written verbatim as the workspace file's settings["window.title"], so VS Code title variables like ${activeEditorShort} pass through. Empty means the repo name.

window_color.description: Colors each worktree window's title bar and status bar via workbench.colorCustomizations in the generated workspace file. "auto" derives a stable color from the repo and branch; "#rrggbb" uses that color everywhere. Requires workspace_file.

workspace_paths.description: Extra folders added to generated .code-workspace files, after the worktree itself. A repos entry or .thrc replaces this list rather than adding to it.

workspace_path.description: One extra folder for generated .code-workspace files.

name.description: The folder's display name in VS Code. Optional.

path.description: The folder's location; a leading ~ expands to the home directory, anything else is written as given.

full_paths.description: Show absolute paths in human-facing output instead of abbreviating the home directory to ~. Same effect as --full-paths.

auto_cd.description: Ask the th shell wrapper (see `th shell-init`) to cd into a worktree `th add` creates. True unless set to false: installing the wrapper is the real opt-in, and without it the setting has no effect. Never applies when the add opens VS Code — the open wins and the terminal stays put.

pre_create.description: Commands run in the main worktree before `th add` creates a worktree, in order, via sh -c, with TH_WORKTREE pointing at the not-yet-existing target. TH_WORKTREE, TH_MAIN, TH_REPO and TH_BRANCH arrive as environment variables, never interpolated into the command. The first failure aborts the add. A repos entry or .thrc replaces this list rather than adding to it; [] clears it. Commands from this user-owned file run as they are; the same key in a repo's .thrc needs approval first.

post_create.description: Commands run inside a newly created worktree, in order, via sh -c, with TH_WORKTREE, TH_MAIN, TH_REPO and TH_BRANCH as environment variables. A failure is reported but the worktree survives. A repos entry or .thrc replaces this list rather than adding to it; [] clears it. Commands from this user-owned file run as they are; the same key in a repo's .thrc needs approval first.

pre_remove.description: Commands run inside a worktree about to be removed, in order, via sh -c, with TH_WORKTREE, TH_MAIN, TH_REPO and TH_BRANCH as environment variables. The first failure blocks the removal. A repos entry or .thrc replaces this list rather than adding to it; [] clears it. Commands from this user-owned file run as they are; the same key in a repo's .thrc needs approval first.

post_remove.description: Commands run in the main worktree after a worktree is removed, in order, via sh -c, with TH_WORKTREE pointing at the now-deleted path and TH_MAIN, TH_REPO and TH_BRANCH alongside it. A failure is reported but the removal stands. A repos entry or .thrc replaces this list rather than adding to it; [] clears it. Commands from this user-owned file run as they are; the same key in a repo's .thrc needs approval first.

run.description: The repository's one foreground command for `th run` — a dev server, a test watcher — executed via sh -c in the current worktree's root with the terminal's stdio attached. Compound commands come free via sh -c. TH_WORKTREE, TH_MAIN, TH_REPO and TH_BRANCH arrive as environment variables, never interpolated into the command. Empty falls through to the layer below. A command from this user-owned file runs as it is; a command supplied by a repo's .thrc needs approval first.
